title: Agent Skills, Files API & Managed Agents
content:
## Overview

Through mid-2026, Anthropic moved three previously-beta capabilities — **computer use**, the **Skills API**, and the **Files API** — to general availability on the Claude Developer Platform, and expanded **Managed Agents** (still beta) with new operational controls. Together these let a developer build agents that operate software the way a person would, apply an organization's own expertise via reusable skills, and hand back finished files rather than just text. This page covers each piece and how they compose.

---

## Agent Skills

An **Agent Skill** is a folder of instructions, scripts, and templates that Claude loads only when a task actually calls for it — keeping the base system prompt lean while still giving Claude deep, specific procedural knowledge on demand.

- **Pre-built skills:** Anthropic ships ready-made skills for common document tasks — PowerPoint (`.pptx`), Excel (`.xlsx`), Word (`.docx`), and PDF generation/editing. (Claude Code exposes these as the `pptx`, `xlsx`, `docx`, and `pdf` skills.)
- **Custom skills:** A custom skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file (instructions in Markdown, with metadata like a name and trigger description) plus any supporting files — scripts, reference docs, templates. You upload it to your workspace either as a zip archive or as individual files, and it becomes available to Claude the same way a built-in skill is.
- **Skills API:** Programmatic access to create, list, and manage custom skills for a workspace, so skills can be versioned and deployed like any other application asset rather than pasted into prompts by hand.

---

## Files API

The Files API lets an agent read and write files as first-class objects in a conversation rather than only as inline base64 blobs or plain text. Combined with computer use and Skills, this is what allows an agent to, for example, open a spreadsheet skill, edit a workbook, and return the finished `.xlsx` file directly — rather than describing the changes in prose.

---

## Managed Agents (beta)

**Managed Agents** is an Anthropic-hosted surface for running stateful, server-managed agents without operating your own orchestration loop:

- **Per-session sandboxes:** Each agent session gets its own container as a workspace; the agent's tool calls — bash commands, file operations, code execution — run inside that container.
- **Anthropic-hosted orchestration:** The agent loop itself runs on Anthropic's infrastructure, not the caller's; the caller configures the agent (system prompt, tools, skills) and the sandbox executes its actions.
- **Persistent agent configs:** An agent's configuration (skills, tools, instructions) can persist across sessions rather than being redefined on every call.

### New controls added in the August 2026 platform update

- **Web access controls** — fine-grained settings for whether and how a Managed Agent session can reach the open internet.
- **Self-hosted sandbox memory stores** — an organization can host the persistent memory/state store for its agents' sandboxes itself, rather than relying solely on Anthropic-hosted storage.
- **Redesigned Console session viewer** — richer observability into a running or completed Managed Agent session (tool calls, sandbox activity, timing) directly in the Claude Console.

---

## Related Platform Changes

Alongside these, the Admin API's user management functionality reached general availability in the same update, giving organizations programmatic control over workspace membership and roles — relevant for teams rolling out Managed Agents or custom Skills across many users.

---

## How This Fits Together

A typical agent built on these primitives: a Managed Agent session spins up a sandbox, loads a relevant custom Skill (e.g., "generate a quarterly report"), uses computer use or direct tool calls to gather data, and returns a finished document through the Files API — all without the caller managing infrastructure or writing an agent loop themselves. This is a more "batteries-included" alternative to the DIY tool-use pattern described on the Tool Use & Agents page, aimed at teams that want Anthropic to host the agent runtime rather than building it into their own product.
